data.one_liner: Allows using the Provider package with AsyncRedux instead of traditional connector widgets.
data.what_it_does: Bridges AsyncRedux and Provider by providing AsyncReduxProvider, ReduxConsumer, and ReduxSelector. This allows injecting and consuming the Redux store, state, and dispatch methods using Provider patterns instead of standard connector widgets.
use_when: You want to use AsyncRedux for state management while leveraging Provider for dependency injection or widget consumption.
You are migrating a project between AsyncRedux and Provider-based architectures.
avoid_when: You are using standard Redux or other state management solutions like Bloc or Riverpod without AsyncRedux.
You prefer using standard AsyncRedux connector widgets over Provider.
strengths: Seamless integration between Provider and AsyncRedux.
Reduces boilerplate by removing the need for traditional connector widgets.
Supports fine-grained rebuilds using ReduxConsumer and ReduxSelector.
weaknesses: Strictly tied to AsyncRedux and Provider ecosystem versions.
Requires learning AsyncRedux conventions alongside Provider.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding async_redux and provider dependencies alongside this package.

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer the BLoC pattern for state management instead of Redux.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a modern compile-safe dependency injection and state management solution.

data.minimal_example: Widget build(BuildContext context) => AsyncReduxProvider<AppState>.value(value: store, child: MaterialApp(home: MyHomePage()));
